title: Inference servers, now: Ollama, vLLM and llama.cpp as hardened services
part: Part 2 · Linux under AI systems, then and now
brief: A model server is a memory-hungry network service that runs what it is asked. Localhost, a cgroup ceiling, a sandbox, the GPU and nothing else.

exercises.prompt: The course's Ollama unit override sets OLLAMA_HOST to which address, and why?
options: 127.0.0.1:11434, because about 175,000 Ollama instances were found publicly exposed in 2026
exercises.explain: Localhost only. Containers reach it through host.docker.internal via the egress proxy. Most exposed instances are someone's homelab with a model that will run whatever it is asked.

exercises.prompt: The Ollama unit has MemoryMax=48G and MemoryHigh=44G. The same host runs kind and the agent. What is the point?
options: The model is what gets throttled first, not kubelet
It stops the model from loading
exercises.explain: cgroup v2 decides who starves. MemoryHigh throttles the model before MemoryMax kills it, and kubelet keeps running. systemd-cgtop and /proc/pressure show it happening.

exercises.prompt: Fix this Ollama drop-in: localhost only, MemoryHigh below MemoryMax, no privilege gain, a read-only system with the model store writable, and only the NVIDIA device nodes reachable.
exercises.hint: OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434; swap the memory values so MemoryHigh (44G) is below MemoryMax (48G); add NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/ollama, PrivateTmp=yes, DevicePolicy=closed and DeviceAllow=/dev/nvidiactl rw, /dev/nvidia-uvm rw, /dev/nvidia0 rw.
exercises.explain: This is a trimmed version of what setup/01-ollama-systemd.sh writes. With DevicePolicy=closed the service sees only the devices you list, so the GPU works and nothing else under /dev does.

exercises.prompt: `docker run --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi` fails with 'could not select device driver "" with capabilities: [[gpu]]'. Why?
options: The NVIDIA Container Toolkit is not installed or not configured for Docker (nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker, then restart Docker)
exercises.explain: Docker cannot reach GPUs by itself; the toolkit injects the driver libraries and device nodes into the container. --privileged exposes every device on the host and is never the fix.

exercises.prompt: vLLM starts and immediately takes about 90% of the GPU's memory before any request. What is happening?
options: By design: --gpu-memory-utilization defaults to 0.9 and vLLM pre-allocates its KV cache; lower it when the GPU is shared
exercises.explain: vLLM reserves memory up front so its paged KV cache never has to ask for more mid-request. On a shared GPU, set --gpu-memory-utilization to the share this server should own.

exercises.prompt: Tokens per second halved overnight; nvidia-smi still shows 100% GPU utilization. What do you check first?
options: Why the clocks are throttled: nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE lists the reasons (power cap, thermal, slowdown)
exercises.explain: Utilization only says a kernel was running, not how fast. A hot or power-capped GPU shows the same 100% at lower clocks; temperature, power draw and the throttle reasons tell you which.

exercises.prompt: Watch GPU utilization and memory per process, live, in the terminal.
exercises.explain: nvtop is the htop of GPUs (NVIDIA, AMD and Intel). nvidia-smi pmon and dmon stream per-process and per-device samples without installing anything.
